original_interpretation: MOFCOM Announcement 2025 No. 62 (9 October 2025, effective on issuance) controlled exports of rare-earth mining, separation, smelting, magnet-making and recycling technologies, and barred Chinese citizens and entities from giving substantive unlicensed support to such activities abroad.
evidence_found: "（一）稀土开采、冶炼分离、金属冶炼、磁材制造、稀土二次资源回收利用相关技术及其载体" ... "七、中国公民、法人、非法人组织未经许可不得为境外稀土开采……活动提供任何实质性帮助和支持" ... "八、本公告自发布之日起实施。" (Announcement 2025 No. 62, dated 2025-10-09)
notes: Re-opened the MOFCOM notice. Date, scope, effective-on-issuance and para. 7 all match. Context: suspended by Announcement 2025 No. 70 from 7 Nov 2025 to 10 Nov 2026 (CLM-1396). claim_type fact and source_type regulator are right.

original_interpretation: MOFCOM/GACC Announcement 2025 No. 55 (9 October 2025) would have controlled superhard materials from 8 November 2025, including synthetic diamond micropowder, diamond wire saws and grinding wheels meeting set specifications, and DC arc plasma CVD equipment and process technology.
evidence_found: "一、2C902.a．平均粒径小于等于50 μm的人造金刚石微粉" ... "三、2C902.c．具有以下所有特性的人造金刚石线锯" ... "四、2C902.d．……人造金刚石砂轮" ... "五、2B005.b．直流电弧等离子体喷射化学气相沉积（DCPCVD）设备" "六、2E902 ……（DCPCVD）工艺技术" ... "本公告自2025年11月8日起正式实施。" (dated 2025-10-09)
notes: Matches. The notice also covers 2C902.b synthetic single-crystal diamond 50-500 μm (lab-grown jewellery diamonds excluded), not mentioned in the claim. 'Would have' is correct: suspended by No. 70 before 8 Nov 2025.

original_interpretation: MOFCOM/GACC Announcement 2025 No. 57 (9 October 2025) would have added export controls on holmium, erbium, thulium, europium and ytterbium items from 8 November 2025.
evidence_found: "一、1C909 钬相关物项" "二、1C910 铒相关物项" "三、1C911 铥相关物项" "四、1C912 铕相关物项" "五、1C913 镱相关物项" ... "本公告自2025年11月8日起正式实施。" (Announcement 2025 No. 57, dated 2025-10-09)
notes: Holmium, erbium, thulium, europium, ytterbium items (metals, alloys, targets, oxides, compounds) confirmed. Suspended by No. 70 before taking effect.

original_interpretation: On 9 October 2025 China's Unreliable Entity List working mechanism listed TechInsights Inc. and nine affiliates (including Strategy Analytics entities), together with 13 US defence-related entities, banning them from China-related import/export and new investment in China, and banning Chinese parties from transacting with them or sending them data.
evidence_found: "决定将反无人机技术公司、TechInsights公司及其分支机构等外国实体列入不可靠实体清单"; measures "一、禁止上述实体从事与中国有关的进出口活动；二、禁止上述实体在中国境内新增投资；三、……特别是向上述实体传输数据、提供敏感信息。" Annex items 1-13 incl. "12. Recorded Future公司" "13. 哈利法克斯国际安全论坛"; item 14 TechInsights Inc. + 9 sub-entities.
notes: Measures, date and the TechInsights + 9 affiliates count are right. The notice does not describe the other 13 as US or defence-related; at least Recorded Future (threat intelligence) and the Halifax International Security Forum are not defence firms. Superseding claim added.
correction: The other 13 listed entities are not described as 'US defence-related' in the notice; they include Recorded Future and the Halifax International Security Forum. Total listed: 13 organisations + TechInsights Inc. and 9 affiliates (23 entities).

original_interpretation: MOFCOM/GACC Announcement 2025 No. 70 (7 November 2025) suspended Announcements 2025 Nos. 55, 56, 57, 58, 61 and 62 from that day until 10 November 2026.
evidence_found: "经批准，自即日起至2026年11月10日，商务部、海关总署公告2025年第55号、56号、57号、58号，及商务部公告2025年第61号、62号暂停实施。" (Announcement 2025 No. 70, dated 2025-11-07)
notes: Exact match. Tier-1 confirmation of CLM-0349.

original_interpretation: MOFCOM Announcement 2025 No. 72 (9 November 2025) suspended paragraph 2 of Announcement 2024 No. 46 (the US-specific gallium/germanium/antimony/superhard ban and graphite review) until 27 November 2026; paragraph 1 (ban on US military users) was not suspended.
evidence_found: "经批准，自即日起至2026年11月27日，商务部公告2024年第46号（《关于加强相关两用物项对美国出口管制的公告》）第二款暂停实施。" (Announcement 2025 No. 72, dated 2025-11-09). No. 46 para. 2: "原则上不予许可镓、锗、锑、超硬材料相关两用物项对美国出口；对石墨两用物项对美国出口，实施更严格的最终用户和最终用途审查。"
notes: Re-opened both notices. Only para. 2 is suspended, so para. 1 (ban on US military users/uses) stays, as the claim says. Not addressed: No. 46's closing third-country liability sentence. USGS MCS 2026 describes the same event as China 'lifted its ban on gallium exports to the United States for 1 year'.

original_interpretation: MOFCOM said that from 10 November 2025 China stopped export-control-list measures against the 15 US entities of Announcement 2025 No. 13 and suspended for another year those against the 16 US entities of Announcement 2025 No. 21; exports to them now require a licence application.
evidence_found: "中方决定自2025年11月10日起，对第13号公告的15家美国实体停止上述相关措施；对第21号公告的16家美国实体继续暂停上述相关措施1年。出口经营者如需向上述实体出口两用物项，应当根据《中华人民共和国两用物项出口管制条例》相关规定向商务部提出申请" (MOFCOM spokesperson, 2025-11-05)
notes: Exact match. Source is a spokesperson Q&A announcing a government decision; 'fact' is acceptable since it is MOFCOM announcing its own measure.

original_interpretation: MOFCOM said that from 10 November 2025 China stopped the Unreliable Entity List measures of 4 March 2025 (notices 2025 Nos. 5 and 6) and suspended for another year the measures of 4 April 2025 (notice 2025 No. 7), to implement the Kuala Lumpur consensus.
evidence_found: "为落实中美吉隆坡经贸磋商共识，中方决定自2025年11月10日起，继续暂停4月4日公告（不可靠实体清单工作机制公告〔2025〕7号）相关措施1年，停止3月4日公告（不可靠实体清单工作机制公告〔2025〕5号和6号）相关措施。" (MOFCOM spokesperson, 2025-11-05)
notes: Exact match. Covers only the March/April 2025 US listings; the 9 Oct 2025 UEL notice 〔2025〕10号 (TechInsights etc.) is not mentioned.

original_interpretation: MOFCOM blamed the Nexperia supply disruption on the Dutch government's 30 September 2025 order, a Dutch Enterprise Chamber ruling stripping the Chinese owner's rights, and Nexperia Netherlands' 26 October 2025 halt of wafer supply to Nexperia China.
evidence_found: "荷兰政府9月30日发布行政令，不当干预安世半导体企业内部事务，之后荷企业法庭作出剥夺中国企业股权的错误裁决……安世（荷兰）10月26日宣布停止向安世（中国）供应晶圆，导致后者无法正常生产……对此，荷方应承担全部责任。" (MOFCOM spokesperson, 2025-11-04)
notes: Correctly recorded as MOFCOM's account (reported_claim). MOFCOM calls the ruling one 'stripping the Chinese company's equity'; Nexperia's own 14 Oct 2025 account says the Enterprise Chamber suspended the CEO and placed substantially all Wingtech-held voting rights under an administrator, which is narrower than stripping equity.

original_interpretation: MOFCOM said that on 1 November 2025 China announced exemptions for qualifying exports related to Nexperia, assessed case by case on companies' actual circumstances.
evidence_found: SRC-0461 (2025-11-01): "我们将综合考虑企业实际情况，对符合条件的出口予以豁免。"; SRC-0462 (2025-11-04): "中方……于11月1日宣布将对符合条件的出口予以豁免，并努力促进安世（中国）恢复供货。"
notes: Both passages found; the 1 Nov statement is in the context of Nexperia.

original_interpretation: MOFCOM said the gallium and germanium controls do not target any specific country, that export control does not prohibit exports, and that it gave prior notice through the China-US and China-EU export control dialogues.
evidence_found: Shu Jueting: "It should be noted that export control does not prohibit exports, and exports that meet the relevant regulations will be allowed. ... China's measure does not target any specific country, and prior notifications had been provided through channels such as the China-U.S. and China-EU export control dialogues before the notice was issued." (MOFCOM Regular Press Conference, 6 July 2023)
notes: Verbatim match. Correctly a reported_claim (the ministry describing its own measure).

original_interpretation: By late 2023 MOFCOM said it had approved some gallium and germanium export applications but gave no numbers.
evidence_found: "Since the implementation of these control measures from August 1, MOFCOM has received applications from enterprises for the exportation of gallium and germanium related items. We have approved after review some of the export applications, and some companies have obtained export licenses for dual-use items." (MOFCOM Regular Press Conference, 30 Nov 2023)
notes: Verbatim match; no counts given. 'Late 2023' = 30 November 2023. Source title in the DB says the conference is about graphite; it covers graphite, gallium and germanium.

original_interpretation: Asked in December 2025 how many rare-earth export licences had been approved since late October, MOFCOM gave no number and said all compliant civilian applications had been promptly approved.
evidence_found: "Q: Since late October, how many companies have received Chinese government's approval for rare earth export licenses? ... A: Regarding your question on rare earth export licenses, I have already addressed this issue. I would like to reiterate that all compliant export applications for civilian purposes have been promptly approved by the Chinese government." (MOFCOM press conference, 4 Dec 2025)
notes: Substance verified (no number; all compliant civilian applications promptly approved). Small wording error about the question.
correction: The question asked how many companies had received approval, not how many licences had been approved.

original_interpretation: MOFCOM Announcement 2026 No. 1 (6 January 2026) banned all dual-use exports to Japanese military users and uses, and to any end user or use that helps raise Japan's military strength.
evidence_found: "禁止所有两用物项对日本军事用户、军事用途，以及一切有助于提升日本军事实力的其他最终用户用途出口。" ... "本公告自公布之日起正式实施。" (Announcement 2026 No. 1, dated 2026-01-06)
notes: Exact match. The notice also makes any party anywhere liable for transferring Chinese-origin dual-use items to Japanese organisations/individuals in breach of the ban.

original_interpretation: On 7 January 2026 MOFCOM opened an anti-dumping investigation into dichlorosilane (DCS) from Japan, a gas used for thin-film deposition in logic, memory and analog chip manufacturing, after a petition by Tangshan Sunfar Electronic Materials.
evidence_found: "商务部……于2025年12月8日收到唐山三孚电子材料有限公司……提交的反倾销调查申请" ... "商务部决定自2026年1月7日起对原产于日本的进口二氯二氢硅进行反倾销立案调查" ... "主要用途：二氯二氢硅主要用于芯片制造过程中的薄膜沉积……用于生产逻辑芯片、存储芯片、模拟芯片和其他类芯片" (Announcement 2026 No. 2)
notes: Matches. Dumping period 1 Jul 2024-30 Jun 2025; injury period 2022-1H2025; due to end by 7 Jan 2027 (extendable 6 months). HS 28539090.

original_interpretation: In its 7 September 2026 preliminary determination MOFCOM found dumping of Japanese dichlorosilane and imposed provisional deposits from 8 September 2026 of 99.2% for Shin-Etsu Chemical, 80.8% for Denal Silane, and 99.2% for other Japanese companies.
evidence_found: "调查机关初步认定，原产于日本的进口被调查产品存在倾销" ... "自2026年9月8日起，进口经营者……应……提供相应的保证金" ... "1. 信越化学工业株式会社 99.2 % ... 2. 德纳尔硅烷株式会社 80.8 % ... 3. 其他日本公司 99.2 %" (Announcement 2026 No. 37, dated 2026-09-07)
notes: Exact match. Deposit is ad valorem on the customs dutiable value, multiplied by (1 + import VAT rate). Preliminary determination, not final.

original_interpretation: On 27 March 2026 MOFCOM opened a trade-barrier investigation into US practices that 'damage global supply chains', including restrictions or bans on exports of high-tech products to China, due to finish within six months (extendable by up to three).
evidence_found: "美国在贸易相关领域实施了大量严重破坏全球产供链的做法和措施，包括但不限于：……限制或禁止高新技术产品对华出口" ... "商务部决定自2026年3月27日起对美国相关做法和措施启动贸易壁垒调查" ... "本案应当自立案决定公告之日起6个月内结束，特殊情况下可以延长，但延长期不得超过3个月。" (Announcement 2026 No. 17)
notes: Accurate as a description of the opening notice. Newer: Xinhua (30 Sep 2026) reports MOFCOM extended the investigation to 27 December 2026 (the full 3-month extension); added as a new claim. Not marked outdated because the claim describes the notice's terms.

original_interpretation: On 2 May 2026 MOFCOM issued its first published blocking prohibition under the Blocking Rules, ordering that US SDN sanctions on five Chinese refiners over Iranian oil must not be recognised, enforced or complied with.
evidence_found: "不得承认、不得执行、不得遵守美国依据第13902号行政令、第13846号行政令等规定，以参与伊朗石油交易为由，对恒力石化（大连）炼化有限公司、山东寿光鲁清石化有限公司、山东金诚石化集团有限公司、河北鑫海化工集团有限公司和山东胜星化工有限公司采取的列入'特别指定国民清单'……等制裁措施。" (Announcement 2026 No. 21, 2026-05-02). Fangda: "这是自2021年1月9日《阻断办法》公布以来，中国商务部第一次……发布阻断禁令".
notes: Everything except 'first' is verified against the MOFCOM notice. The notice itself does not say 'first'; Fangda Partners commentary (tier 3, opened this run) says it is. Added as a separate claim.
correction: 'First published blocking prohibition' is supported only by Fangda Partners law-firm commentary (6 May 2026), not by the MOFCOM notice.

original_interpretation: On 22 June 2026 MOFCOM put 10 US entities on its export-control control list, including rare-earth producers MP Materials Corp. and USA Rare Earth, Inc., banning dual-use exports to them and banning any party anywhere from transferring Chinese-origin dual-use items to them.
evidence_found: "决定将艾维奥克斯公司等10家美国实体列入出口管制管控名单" ... "一、禁止出口经营者对上述10家实体出口两用物项，禁止任何国家和地区的组织和个人将原产于中国的两用物项转移或提供给上述实体" ... "9. 芒廷帕斯材料公司（MP Materials Corp.）" "10. 美国稀土公司（USA Rare Earth, Inc.）" (Announcement 2026 No. 23, 2026-06-22)
notes: Matches. Calling them 'rare-earth producers' comes from the researcher, not the notice, which gives only names and addresses; that description was not checked here. Most of the other 8 are defence, aerospace or drone firms (e.g. Red Cat, Teal Drones, Oshkosh Defense, L3Harris Maritime).

original_interpretation: MOFCOM issued Measures for Industrial and Supply Chain Security Investigations (Announcement 2026 No. 24, 22 June 2026) under State Council Decree No. 834, letting it investigate foreign measures or firms that damage China's supply chains and respond with import/export bans, special fees, countermeasure listing, and investment bans.
evidence_found: "为贯彻落实《国务院关于产业链供应链安全的规定》（国务院令第834号）……商务部制定了《产业链供应链安全调查工作办法》" (Announcement 2026 No. 24, dated 2026-06-22). Art. 17: "（一）禁止或者限制与其有关的货物、技术进出口……（二）对与其有关的活动收取特别费用；（三）……列入反制清单"; Art. 18(2): "禁止或者限制其在我国境内投资".
notes: Matches. Art. 3 covers foreign states' discriminatory measures and foreign organisations or individuals that cut off normal trade with Chinese parties. Investment bans are under Art. 18 (foreign organisations/individuals), not Art. 17. Published 24 June 2026.

original_interpretation: From 1 July 2026 MOFCOM runs a whistleblower system for strategic-mineral export-control violations, covering third-country rerouting, splitting items into parts to evade licensing, and trading with listed end users, with rewards for verified real-name reports.
evidence_found: "（四）以改造、拆分为部件或者组件等方式规避许可……（五）通过绕道第三国（地区）规避……（九）出口经营者违反规定与列入管控名单的进口商、最终用户进行交易" ... "对查证属实的，商务部按有关规定可给予实名举报者奖励。" ... "本公告自2026年7月1日起正式实施。" (Announcement 2026 No. 26, 2026-06-24)
notes: Matches. Rewards are discretionary ('可给予'). Also invites voluntary self-disclosure as a mitigating factor.

original_interpretation: On 24 July 2026 MOFCOM put 14 EU entities on its export-control control list, including III-V Lab (France) and Vigo Photonics (Poland), both compound-semiconductor/photonics organisations.
evidence_found: "决定将拉法特集团等14家欧盟实体列入出口管制管控名单" ... "7.三五实验室（III-V LAB）……Palaiseau, France" ... "9.维戈尔光电公司（Vigo Photonics S.A.）……Poland" (Announcement 2026 No. 30, 2026-07-24). III-V Lab: "an industrial research lab in Photonics and Microelectronics, where III-V alloys are created"; VIGO: "European manufacturer of epitaxial wafers and instruments for photonics and microelectronics".
notes: The listing is verified against the notice. The researcher's description of both as compound-semiconductor/photonics organisations is confirmed by their own websites (company_documentation).

original_interpretation: The White House said in November 2025 that China would issue general licences for exports of rare earths, gallium, germanium, antimony and graphite for the benefit of US end users, calling this the de facto removal of controls imposed since 2023.
evidence_found: "China will issue general licenses valid for exports of rare earths, gallium, germanium, antimony, and graphite for the benefit of U.S. end users and their suppliers around the world. The general license means the de facto removal of controls China imposed since 2023." (White House fact sheet, Nov 2025)
notes: Verbatim match. Correctly a reported_claim (one government describing the other's commitment). No Chinese general-licence notice was found in this run. The Sept 2026 fact sheet says rare-earth shipment levels had still not returned to appropriate levels (CLM-1402).

original_interpretation: The White House said in November 2025 that China would end its investigations targeting US companies in the semiconductor supply chain, including antitrust, anti-monopoly and anti-dumping investigations.
evidence_found: "China will terminate its various investigations targeting U.S. companies in the semiconductor supply chain, including its antitrust, anti-monopoly, and anti-dumping investigations." (White House fact sheet, Nov 2025)
notes: Verbatim match. Whether China actually ended these (e.g. the analog-chip anti-dumping case, Announcement 2025 No. 27) was not checked.

original_interpretation: The White House said China would suspend or remove non-tariff countermeasures taken since 4 March 2025, including listing US companies on its end-user and unreliable entity lists.
evidence_found: "China will suspend or remove all of the retaliatory non-tariff countermeasures taken against the United States since March 4, 2025, including China's listing of certain American companies on its end user and unreliable entity lists." (White House fact sheet, Nov 2025)
notes: Verbatim match (the claim leaves out 'all of'). Consistent with MOFCOM's 5 Nov 2025 actions (CLM-1409, CLM-1410).

original_interpretation: The White House said in November 2025 that China would take measures to resume trade from Nexperia's facilities in China so that legacy chips could flow to the rest of the world.
evidence_found: "China will take appropriate measures to ensure the resumption of trade from Nexperia's facilities in China, allowing production of critical legacy chips to flow to the rest of the world." (White House fact sheet, Nov 2025)
notes: Verbatim match.

original_interpretation: In May 2026 the White House said China would address US concerns about shortages of rare earths and critical minerals including yttrium, scandium, neodymium and indium, and about restrictions on selling rare-earth production equipment and technology.
evidence_found: "China will address U.S. concerns regarding supply chain shortages related to rare earths and other critical minerals, including yttrium, scandium, neodymium, and indium. China will also address U.S. concerns regarding prohibitions or restrictions on the sale of rare earth production and processing equipment and technologies." (White House fact sheet, May 2026)
notes: Verbatim match.

original_interpretation: As of 25 September 2026 the White House said the US and China were still working on US concerns about rare-earth and critical-mineral shortages, aiming to return shipments to appropriate levels.
evidence_found: "The United States and China continue to work on U.S. concerns regarding supply chain shortages related to rare earths and other critical minerals, with the goal of ensuring shipment levels return to appropriate levels." (White House fact sheet on Xi state visit, Sept 2026)
notes: Verbatim match. The page text shows no date; the URL path (2026/09) and the DB record (2026-09-25) agree, and press coverage of the fact sheet is dated 26 Sep 2026.

original_interpretation: Nexperia said that on 4 October 2025 MOFCOM issued an export control notice prohibiting Nexperia China and its subcontractors from exporting specific finished components and sub-assemblies made in China.
evidence_found: "On 4 October 2025, the Chinese Ministry of Commerce issued an export control notice prohibiting Nexperia China and its subcontractors from exporting specific finished components and sub-assemblies manufactured in China." (Nexperia, 'Update on company developments', 14 Oct 2025)
notes: Verbatim match; correctly a reported_claim (the company's account). The MOFCOM notice itself was not found.

original_interpretation: Nexperia linked the dispute to a 29 September 2025 BIS rule extending US Entity List restrictions to entities at least 50% owned by listed parties, which affected it as a wholly owned subsidiary of Wingtech.
evidence_found: "On 29 September 2025, the United States Bureau of Industry and Security ('BIS') issued a rule extending US export control restrictions to entities at least 50% owned by one or more entities on the US Entity List. Although Nexperia is not explicitly mentioned, the company is affected due to its status as a wholly owned subsidiary of Wingtech ... that was put on the BIS entity list last December." (Nexperia, 14 Oct 2025)
notes: Verbatim match. Later context: the White House Nov 2025 fact sheet says the US would suspend this 'Affiliates' rule for one year from 10 Nov 2025.

original_interpretation: BBC News reported that the exemptions were for exports made by Nexperia for civilian use, easing carmakers' fears of production stoppages in Europe.
evidence_found: "Exemptions have been granted to exports made by Chinese-owned Nexperia for civilian use, it said, which should help carmakers who had feared production in Europe would be hit." (BBC News, 'China exempts chips used by carmakers from export curbs')
notes: Close paraphrase, correctly attributed. BBC is reporting China's commerce ministry statement; tier-3 news. The article gives no explicit date ('on Sunday', after Sefcovic's Saturday post, i.e. around 9 Nov 2025).

original_interpretation: USGS reported that China's exports of germanium metal in January-August 2024 fell 55% year on year to 16,700 kg after the August 2023 licensing requirement.
evidence_found: "In August 2023, the Government of China implemented an export licensing program for germanium. China's reported exports of germanium metal for the year through August 2024 decreased by 55% to 16,700 kilograms compared with those in the same period in 2023." (USGS MCS 2025, Germanium, Events, Trends, and Issues)
notes: Value, unit, period and population all match. USGS is quoting Chinese reported trade data.

original_interpretation: USGS described Announcement 2024 No. 46 as China banning all germanium exports to the United States in December 2024.
evidence_found: "In December 2024, China banned all exports of germanium to the United States." (USGS MCS 2025, Germanium)
notes: Verified as a description of what USGS wrote. Legally, No. 46 para. 2 says 原则上不予许可 ('in principle not licensed'), which is softer than a total ban. That para. was suspended from 9 Nov 2025 to 27 Nov 2026 (CLM-1385). USGS MCS 2026 (gallium) records the November 2025 lifting.

original_interpretation: USGS estimated China accounted for 99% of world primary low-purity gallium production in 2024.
evidence_found: "China accounted for 99% of worldwide primary low-purity gallium production." (USGS MCS 2025, Gallium); table 'World Low-Purity Production': China 2024e 750,000 kg of world total 760,000 kg.
notes: Text matches; the table gives 750/760 = 98.7% for 2024e, so 99% is a rounded figure. The newer MCS 2026 repeats 99% (added as a new claim), so the figure is not outdated.

original_interpretation: A USGS study (Nov 2024, as cited by the Stimson Center) estimated that a total Chinese ban on gallium and germanium exports could raise gallium prices by 150% and germanium prices by 26% and cut US GDP by USD 3.4 billion.
evidence_found: Stimson: "The USGS has estimated such a total ban could cause a 150% increase in price for gallium and a 26% increase for germanium and constrain supply, leading to a $3.4 billion decrease in U.S. GDP." Primary OFR 2024-1057: gallium prices "increase by more than 2.5-fold"; germanium "increase by 26 percent"; GDP "$3.4 billion ($1.7 billion to $9.0 billion) if disrupted simultaneously."
notes: Stimson quote is verbatim, and the original USGS report matches it. The primary report adds that the scenario is a complete restriction of China's net exports (2022 baseline) and gives a range. A primary-sourced superseding claim was added. The USGS news release URL was blocked; the OFR publication page was opened instead.

original_interpretation: The Stimson Center, using China Customs data, argued that falling direct Chinese gallium/germanium exports to the US were partly offset by reexport through third countries.
evidence_found: "all analysis of China's exports relies on data from China's General Administration of Customs"; "Though Chinese data shows that no exports of germanium or gallium went to the United States in 2024, U.S. trade data tells a different story, showing 26% of its germanium imports (about 3,500kg) and 8% of its gallium imports (900kg) still came from China"; "For gallium, the potential for reexport is more clouded by the possibility of increased secondary production"; "As we have seen, reexport helps."
notes: The argument exists, but (1) it rests on comparing China customs data with US Census import data, not on China customs data alone; (2) it is strong for germanium (via Belgium) and explicitly uncertain for gallium. claim_type 'estimate' is loose: this is a think-tank's analytical argument, and reported_claim or interpretation would be more accurate.
correction: Stimson uses both China GAC export data and US Census import data. The reexport argument is mainly about germanium via Belgium; for gallium Stimson says reexport is 'more clouded' by possible secondary production.

original_interpretation: Decree No. 792 itself sets no numeric value threshold for its extraterritorial rule; the 0.1% value threshold appears in MOFCOM Announcement 2025 No. 61, not in the Decree.
evidence_found: Decree 792 Art. 49: "境外组织和个人在中华人民共和国境外向特定目的国家和地区、特定组织和个人转移、提供下列货物……（一）含有、集成或者混有原产于中华人民共和国的特定两用物项在境外制造的两用物项……" (no percentage anywhere in the decree text retrieved). Announcement 2025 No. 61 para. 1(1): "……价值比例达到0.1%及以上的".
notes: The interpretation follows: the full decree text retrieved has no '%' or value-ratio wording, and the 0.1% de minimis is in Announcement No. 61. Based on CLM-1373 and CLM-1389. Note: No. 61 is suspended until 10 Nov 2026 (CLM-1396).

original_interpretation: The November 2025 suspension (Announcement 2025 No. 70) does not list the April 2025 rare-earth controls (Announcement 2025 No. 18), so those controls appear to remain in force.
evidence_found: Announcement 2025 No. 70: "……商务部、海关总署公告2025年第55号、56号、57号、58号，及商务部公告2025年第61号、62号暂停实施。" No. 18 is not named. White House May 2026: "...shortages related to rare earths and other critical minerals, including yttrium, scandium..."
notes: The inference follows from the text, which suspends only the listed notices, and is suitably hedged ('appear'). The yttrium/scandium shortages named in May 2026 (both No. 18 elements) fit this reading. Caveat: the White House says China committed to general licences for US end users, which could ease No. 18 in practice without repealing it.

original_interpretation: Since 2026 MOFCOM control-list notices (e.g. 2026 Nos. 23, 27 and 30) ban not only Chinese exporters but also foreign organisations and individuals from transferring Chinese-origin dual-use items to listed entities; the March 2025 notice (2025 No. 13) banned only exports to them.
evidence_found: 2026 No. 23: "禁止任何国家和地区的组织和个人将原产于中国的两用物项转移或提供给上述实体"; 2026 No. 27: "禁止境外组织和个人将原产于中华人民共和国的两用物项转移或提供给上述20家实体"; 2026 No. 30: same wording for 14 entities; 2025 No. 13: "一、禁止向上述15家美国实体出口两用物项"; 2025 No. 1: "一、禁止向上述28家美国实体出口两用物项".
notes: The comparison holds for the notices opened (2026 Nos. 23, 27, 30 vs 2025 Nos. 1, 13). 'Since 2026' is not established: notices between April 2025 and June 2026 were not audited. Country-wide notices already had similar third-party transfer liability wording (2024 No. 46; 2026 No. 1). Narrowed superseding inference added.
correction: Wider wording confirmed in 2026 Nos. 23, 27, 30 and absent from 2025 Nos. 1 and 13. When it first appeared in control-list notices was not established.

original_interpretation: Article 12 of the Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law could expose multinational chip firms that cut off Chinese customers to comply with US export controls to civil suits in Chinese courts.
evidence_found: AFSL Art. 12: "任何组织和个人均不得执行或者协助执行外国国家对我国公民、组织采取的歧视性限制措施。组织和个人违反前款规定，侵害我国公民、组织合法权益的，我国公民、组织可以依法向人民法院提起诉讼，要求其停止侵害、赔偿损失。"
notes: The interpretation is hedged ('could') and follows from the text: Art. 12 applies to 'any organisation or individual' and gives a private right to sue. It depends on US export controls counting as 'discriminatory restrictive measures' (Art. 3), which Chinese authorities assert but no court has confirmed. No case law was found. The 2026 Supply Chain Security Measures (Arts. 18-19) and the first blocking order (2026 No. 21) are related tools.
